summary: HelixBank (Enterprise/Private) requests audit log evidence for Optimize config changes + rollback actions (who/when/what) for compliance
description:
Issue summary
HelixBank security/compliance team is requesting auditable evidence for optimization configuration changes (Optimize knobs: batching/caching/quantization/routing-related controls) and rollback actions in their Redwood Private deployment.

They need this for change-management controls (SOC 2 / internal audit) and asked specifically for:
- Who initiated the change (human + service accounts)
- When the change occurred (UTC timestamp)
- What changed (before/after values, or at minimum a diff)
- Scope / where it was applied (deployment/cluster/region/route/model; tenant)
- Rollback actions: who rolled back, from which version to which version, and the outcome
- Evidence that the audit history is immutable (or at least tamper-evident) and retained per policy
- Ability to export to their SIEM (Splunk) or provide a signed export for audit sampling

Compliance context
Customer is preparing for an internal audit window in early February and wants:
1) immediate stopgap evidence for the last 30 days of Optimize config changes, and
2) confirmation that upcoming “config history + rollback” functionality will include audit events suitable for enterprise audits.

Impact
- Sales/security approval risk: customer is treating this as a hard requirement for production change-management.
- Operational risk: customer experienced a prior latency regression after an optimization change (referenced SUP-2418) and wants defensible rollback evidence.

Current behavior (as of ticket creation)
- Redwood Private has audit logging for some Console actions (auth/login, role changes, API keys), but Optimize config apply/rollback actions are not consistently recorded as first-class audit events.
- There is no customer-visible immutable config version history in Console for Optimize config (work in progress under Safe apply + rollback mechanism project).

Requested outcome
- Provide an interim export containing recent Optimize config change events (including actor and timestamps) OR a documented statement of what is/not currently captured.
- Provide a spec/commitment for audit events that will exist once the Safe apply + rollback mechanism ships, including retention/redaction guidance for Private.

References provided by customer
- Prior incident + need to rollback quickly (internal notes reference SUP-2418)
- Requirement for auditable rollback controls similar to their existing change-management tooling

Internal notes
This aligns directly with the Safe apply + rollback mechanism scope (versioning + auditability + RBAC). We should respond with:
- Clear current-state: what we can export today (and limitations)
- Near-term plan: audit event taxonomy and rollout dates for Phase 1/2
- Private-specific: where audit logs live, export path, and retention configuration

Support owner checklist
- [x] Identify current logging sources that capture Optimize config changes (if any)
- [x] Confirm roadmap + timelines with Security Ops and Console/Platform
- [x] Provide interim evidence package and a written statement of controls
- [x] Document gaps and link customer request to audit event spec Confluence page
comments:
2025-01-14 10:08 UTC — Elliot Price (Reporter)
Opened per HelixBank security request. They want audit evidence for Optimize config changes + rollback actions. Customer asked for an export they can attach to an audit ticket (actor/time/what changed/scope).

2025-01-14 12:02 UTC — Svetlana Petrenko (Assignee)
Thanks — a few clarifying questions to send to HelixBank:
1) Are they asking for Console operator actions only, or also automated changes applied by Redwood Optimize recommendations / scheduled jobs?
2) What’s their retention expectation (e.g., 90 days / 1 year) and required fields?
3) Preferred export format: JSON lines to Splunk HEC, CSV, or signed PDF?
I’ll also pull in Fiona (Security Ops) + Kevin (audit export/retention) to confirm what we can provide immediately for Private.

2025-01-15 08:41 UTC — Elliot Price
Customer reply (summary):
- Needs both operator actions and any “system-applied” changes (service accounts), with clear actor attribution.
- Minimum retention: 1 year.
- Export: JSON (preferred) or CSV OK; they can ingest into Splunk.
- Must include rollback action evidence, even if rollbacks are manual today.
They also asked whether we support immutable/tamper-evident logs in Private or if we can provide an attestation of controls.

2025-01-15 16:20 UTC — Fiona McCarthy
From Security Ops: We can’t claim “immutable” unless backed by WORM/append-only storage in the customer’s environment. For Private, we can support append-only event logs with restricted write permissions, plus guidance for customers to ship logs to their SIEM for immutability. Redaction: ensure secrets aren’t logged; config payload should be diff’d and/or hashed.
We should propose an audit event schema that includes:
- event_type (optimize_config.apply_attempted/applied/failed, optimize_config.rollback_attempted/rolled_back/failed)
- actor_id + actor_type (human/service)
- tenant_id + scope (deployment/cluster/route/model/region)
- version_from/version_to
- request_id/correlation_id
- change_summary (diff) and/or config_hash
- result + error_code
Retention for hosted is set by Redwood; for Private, retention depends on customer storage but we should recommend >= 365d.

2025-01-16 11:05 UTC — Kevin Osei
Audit export/retention (Private): if HelixBank is using our standard private logging stack, we can emit audit events to their configured sink (e.g., Splunk HEC). Today, Optimize config changes aren’t consistently emitted as audit events; we can do a best-effort export from internal service logs if they can provide timeframe + cluster identifiers.
If they need something immediately for the last 30 days, we can:
- provide a one-time export from control plane logs (where available)
- include statement of limitations (may miss changes applied outside the Console path)
Longer-term: align with the Optimize config change audit event spec page and ensure it’s implemented as part of the safe-apply/rollback work.

2025-01-17 09:32 UTC — Dylan Brooks
Console/Tooling update: the Safe apply + rollback mechanism project explicitly includes audit logging + RBAC for apply/rollback. We expect Phase 1 to cover backend version store + basic rollback UI + audit logs. Phase 2 adds diff/preview + canary gates.
We should share the audit event taxonomy draft and confirm that rollbacks will emit dedicated events with version identifiers + correlation IDs.

2025-01-20 14:18 UTC — Svetlana Petrenko
Action plan sent to customer (summary):
1) Immediate: provide a best-effort export for last 30 days of Optimize config change activity we can derive from current logs, including actor when available, timestamps, and affected scope (deployment/route/model). Include explicit caveats.
2) Near-term (Safe apply + rollback): commit to first-class audit events for apply/rollback, with required fields + export path to Splunk for Private.
3) Provide written guidance for Private: recommended append-only storage + shipping to SIEM for tamper-evidence.
Requested from customer: timezone (UTC ok), cluster identifier(s), and confirmation of the audit window dates.

2025-01-22 10:03 UTC — Elliot Price
Customer provided cluster IDs and approved UTC timestamps. Audit window requested: 2024-12-20 through 2025-01-22. They asked we explicitly mark events as “operator initiated” vs “system initiated”.

2025-01-24 18:27 UTC — Svetlana Petrenko
Delivered interim evidence package to HelixBank via support portal:
- JSON export (best-effort) for requested window with:
  - timestamp_utc, actor (where available), actor_type (human/service), action, scope, request_id (when present)
- Short memo: current limitations and what will change with Safe apply + rollback (version IDs, explicit rollback events, consistent actor attribution).
Also shared link/title of our internal audit event taxonomy draft for Optimize config changes and confirmed we will provide an externally consumable version as part of enterprise docs.

Note: current export may not capture config changes applied via older internal tooling paths; memo includes that limitation.

2025-01-28 09:40 UTC — Elliot Price
Customer confirmation: interim package accepted for upcoming audit sampling, with the caveat noted. They requested notification once first-class audit events for Optimize config apply/rollback are GA for Private.

2025-01-29 15:11 UTC — Svetlana Petrenko
Closing as Resolved.
Follow-ups:
- Ensure the Optimize config audit event taxonomy page is finalized and included in customer-facing docs for enterprise/private.
- Track GA readiness with Console/Platform: audit events must include version_from/version_to + diff/config_hash.
- Confirm RBAC role mapping so designated HelixBank operators can view/export audit events (avoid repeat of “rollback button missing” class of issue; see SUP-2431/INT-911).
resolution: Provided interim audit evidence export for last 30 days (best-effort) plus written limitations; confirmed upcoming first-class audit event taxonomy and implementation plan under Safe apply + rollback mechanism. Customer accepted interim package for audit sampling and requested notification at GA for Private.
next_steps: Publish customer-facing documentation for Optimize config apply/rollback audit events (fields, retention, export to SIEM) aligned with internal taxonomy.
Validate Private deployment supports emitting these audit events to Splunk HEC (or other sinks) with clear actor attribution and correlation IDs.
Confirm RBAC mappings for audit log viewing/export and rollback permissions for enterprise/private tenants.
